what is a neural network|A neural network is a computing system inspired by biological neurons. It processes information through interconnected nodes (neurons) to learn patterns.|tech
explain programming|Programming is writing instructions (code) that computers can execute to perform tasks. Common languages include Python, C, JavaScript, and more.|tech
what is python|Python is a high-level, easy-to-read programming language popular for AI, web development, and data science. It's known for its simplicity!|tech
what is gcc |GCC, the GNU Compiler Collection - The GNU Compiler Collection includes front ends for C, Cplusplus, Objective-C, Fortran, Ada, Go, D, Modula-2, and COBOL as well as libraries for these languages (libstdcplusplus,...). GCC was originally written as the compiler for the GNU operating system. The GNU system was developed to be 100% free software, free in the sense that it respects the user's freedom.|tech
what is cplusplus|Cplusplus is a high-level, general-purpose programming language created by Danish computer scientist Bjarne Stroustrup. First released in 1985|tech
what is c|ANSI C, ISO C, and Standard C are successive standards for the C programming language published by the American National Standards Institute (ANSI) and ISO/IEC JTC 1/SC 22/WG 14 of the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) and the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC).|tech
what is ANSI C|ANSI C, ISO C, and Standard C are successive standards for the C programming language published by the American National Standards Institute (ANSI) and ISO/IEC JTC 1/SC 22/WG 14 of the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) and the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC).|tech

# Science
what is photosynthesis|Photosynthesis is how plants convert sunlight into energy using CO2 and water to make glucose and oxygen!|science
what is evolution|Evolution is the process by which species change over time through natural selection!|science
what is the 3rd rock from the sun | Well that is earth |science 
The First Computer Bug was a Real Bug | In 1947, computer pioneer Grace Hopper and her team were working on the Harvard Mark II when they discovered a moth trapped in one of the machine's relays. They removed the insect and taped it into their logbook with the caption: First actual case of bug being found. While the term bug had been used previously in engineering, this event popularized the terms bug and debugging in the context of software. So the 1st one was A real bug after all!|science
Was the first programmer A Woman | Long before the first electronic computer was built, Ada Lovelace, a mathematician in the 1840s, wrote the world's first algorithm. It was intended for Charles Babbage’s Analytical Engine, a theoretical mechanical computer. Because she saw that the machine could do more than just pure math, she is widely considered the first computer programmer. So yes a Woman|science
The origin of the word Algorithm | actually predates modern computers by over a thousand years. It is a Latinized version of the name of the 9th-century Persian mathematician Muhammad ibn Mūsā al-Khwārizmī. He also wrote the foundational book on algebra, titled Al-Jabr, which is where the word algebra comes from.|science 
Computers Used to be Huge and heavy | The first general-purpose electronic computer, the ENIAC (Electronic Numerical Integrator and Computer), was completed in 1945. It occupied 1,800 square feet, used nearly 18,000 vacuum tubes, and weighed more than 27 tons. For comparison, a modern smartphone is thousands of times faster and weighs only a few ounces.|science
Domain names used to be free | Until 1995, you didn't have to pay to register a domain name. It was only after the internet began to commercialize that companies like Network Solutions were granted the right to charge for them, starting at a fee of $100 for two years of registration.|science

The Apollo 11 Computer Had Less Power than a Toaster?| Yes! The Apollo Guidance Computer (AGC) that helped land humans on the moon in 1969 had approximately 64 KB of memory and operated at a speed of 0.043 MHz. Your average modern smartphone is roughly 100 million times more powerful than the computer that navigated to the moon.|history
Python is Named After a Comedy Show| The Python programming language wasn't named after the snake. Its creator, Guido van Rossum, was a huge fan of the British comedy troupe Monty Python's Flying Circus. He wanted a name that was short, unique, and slightly mysterious.|programming

earths Orbit & Rotation| Earth completes a full orbit around the sun in 365.25 days, causing seasons due to its tilt. It rotates on its axis every 23 hours, 56 minutes, and 4 seconds.|SCIENCE 
what is earths Natural Satellite| The Moon is Earth's only natural satellite, which stabilizes the tilt and controls tides.|SCIENCE
Dynamic Features of earth| Tectonic plates are constantly moving, shaping the landscape and creating earthquakes. The magnetic field protects the planet from solar radiation.|SCIENCE
